The Japanese Spanish mackerel, Scomberomorus niphonius, is a commercially valuable scombrid found throughout the northwest Pacific. The ultimate wet weight corresponding to this length approaches 10,758 grams [Wwi = 10,758 grams], a mass that reflects the streamlined, high-performance body plan characteristic of this pelagic predator. At this length, the corresponding wet weight at puberty is roughly 2,100 grams [Wwp = roughly 2,100 grams], a substantial mass that indicates individuals have accumulated sufficient energy reserves to support vitellogenesis and subsequent spawning. Field surveys of the spawning stock in the Sea of Japan reveal that females typically reach this pubertal size during their second or third year of life, after which they join the adult migratory population. The size-based threshold for maturity appears to be relatively consistent across the species range, with minimal latitudinal variation observed in comparative studies.
